answer: Continuous thermal-signature escrow. Each agent identity must continuously emit a hardware-signed thermal trace from a distinct physical device; the signature is derived from a per-chip secret fused at manufacture. A crystal oscillator's drift and die temperature noise are bound into the attestation, so a plume of cloned software cannot reproduce them. A quill of recorded traces replays fail freshness checks. Attacker cost: one physical device per live identity, non-transferable.
